chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Supplication is the shelter of acceptance, just as clouds are the shelter of rain.

key_terms.الإجابة: Acceptance/answer — God's positive response to supplication
key_terms.الدعاء: Du'a — supplication, personal prayer and invocation addressed directly to God
key_terms.السحاب: Clouds — the natural vessel or means through which rain descends
key_terms.كهف: Shelter, cave — the vehicle or vessel through which something is contained and delivered

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of supplication (du'a) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) draws a beautiful analogy between supplication and clouds: just as clouds are the natural vehicle through which rain descends, du'a is the natural vehicle through which divine acceptance and response descend. The teaching encourages the believer to understand du'a not as passive wishful thinking but as the very means God has appointed for the delivery of His answers. In early Shia thought, this hadith was particularly significant in establishing the necessity and efficacy of du'a even in apparent hardship.
